name: Funeral & repatriation (category guide)
summary: Funeral directors and repatriation logistics for foreigners — ICA/police death paperwork, embassy roles, cargo vs escort flights, and why a will / CPF nomination still matters before anyone quotes urn shipping.
body: When a foreign national dies in Singapore, funeral directors coordinate with hospitals, ICA, and (when required) police documentation before cremation, burial, or repatriation of remains. Embassies help with next-of-kin authentication and laissez-passer paperwork — they do not pay bills. Ask quotes to separate local funeral rites, embalming/cremation, airline cargo, escort seats, and destination receiving costs; ‘repatriation packages’ hide which legs are optional. Keep passport, FIN/pass card, and insurance death-benefit contacts findable; banks freeze accounts until probate/letters of administration appear. Pair this directory entry with the death-repatriation guide, wills/CPF nomination guide, and outbound shipping only when household clear-out is also required. This is a category guide, not a ranked funeral-home list.
